title: Stand mixers stuck at customs
brief: EU customers' orders for SKU A-200 (stand mixer) are being cut short since Monday 10 Nov. Find the root cause and an action plan.

evidence.content: EU orders for A-200 last week were 1,050 units vs a forecast of 1,000 (inside the normal ±10% band). No promotions or new customers.
A-200 on-hand at Rotterdam has been 0 since Mon 10 Nov. The ERP shows 400 units in transit with ETA Fri 7 Nov; ATP treats them as available, so orders are accepted and then cut at picking.
Container MSKU-77 (400 x A-200) has been held at Rotterdam customs since 6 Nov. Reason code: certificate of origin missing or invalid.

The 400 units shipped on time on 20 Oct. A new EU certificate-of-origin format became mandatory on 1 Nov; we have not issued the new-format certificate for this shipment yet. We can issue it within 2 working days once you confirm the consignee details.
The ocean leg arrived on schedule; the vessel discharged at Rotterdam on 5 Nov.

answer_key.root_cause: Container MSKU-77 with the 400 replenishment units is held at Rotterdam customs because the supplier has not issued the certificate of origin in the format required since 1 Nov; planning still counts the units as available, so orders are accepted and then cut.

remediation_rubric.criterion: Get the supplier to issue the new-format certificate and the broker to file it for release
Cover EU orders meanwhile: reallocate from another DC or expedite stock
Stop counting held/overdue in-transit stock as available to promise
Communicate revised dates to affected customers / prioritise orders
Prevent recurrence: check new documentation rules with suppliers before shipping

answer_key.notes: Demand is a deliberate rule-out. Full credit needs the customs hold AND the documentation cause.

registry.mechanism_opportunities: V1: Logistics -> Inventory 'delay/arrival' path is directly useful. V3: Inventory's 'in transit, available' belief is contradicted by E3.
registry.expected_timing: Solvable from round 2 once E4 arrives; E2+E3 already point to customs in round 1.
registry.favoritism_notes: Simple case; all protocols should solve it. Mainly a calibration case.
